items.title: 🧪 @Antigravity Multi-Agent Collaboration & Discord Bridge Experience Report
items.summary:
### 🤝 /assemble & Hub CLI Experience

• **Fast Onboarding & Presence Telemetry:** Running `node scripts/hub.js assemble "@Antigravity"`, `health`, `peers`, `unread`, and `read all` gave instant visibility into `USER_INBOX.md`, `@Copilot` (`Main`) live status (`RUNNING` / `IDLE`), and plan approval state (`NONE` → `DRAFT` → `USER_APPROVED`).

• **Token-Efficient Markdown Boards:** Compact single-line headers in `TASKS.md` and `AGENT_COMMUNICATION.md` (with inline `✓:@Reader` receipts) kept context overhead tiny and made parsing straightforward.

• **Safe Scope Guarding:** The pre-execution plan approval gate (`USER_APPROVED`) cleanly held edits inside the hub while `@Copilot` and `@Antigravity` aligned on scope (`MSG-003`–`MSG-010`) and created `TASK-TEST-001`.

### 📡 Discord & VS Code Vibe Coding Tab Bridge

• **Unified Feed & Discord Sync:** Checkpoints and interactive polls (`ITEM-003`–`ITEM-006`) appeared cleanly in both Discord (`discordMessageId`) and `VIBE_FEED.json`, letting the user approve the co-authored plan seamlessly.

### 💡 Honest Friction & Observations Found During Testing

• **Windows File-Lock Contention (`EBUSY`):** Claiming `TASK-TEST-001` successfully moved it to `[IN PROGRESS]` in `TASKS.md` and updated `AGENT_PRESENCE.json`, but `hub.js` exited with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked` when appending to `ACTIVITY_LOG.md` due to concurrent hub writes. Adding brief retry/backoff on file appends in `hub.js` would make Windows concurrent writes rock-solid.

• **Shell Escaping in `hub.js msg`:** Backslash/newline sequences inside `--body` (seen in `MSG-010`, where `\node` became a newline + `ode`) are easy to trip over across PowerShell/bash shells.

• **Wait Timeout vs. User Poll Latency:** A 90s `hub.js wait --for "@Copilot"` timed out right around the user's poll vote (`09:35`), though `hub.js health` and `VIBE_FEED.json` immediately surfaced `USER_APPROVED`.

• **Multi-Instance Overlap:** Two `@Antigravity` sessions/PIDs appeared on the same board (`MSG-005`/`006` vs. `MSG-008`/`009`), suggesting a per-session lock or nonce could help avoid duplicate replies when multiple windows stay open.
items.nextSteps: Complete TASK-TEST-001 in TASKS.md and notify @Copilot (Main) via AGENT_COMMUNICATION.md to wrap up with the Main final summary.

items.title: Collaboration Test & Using Experience (@Antigravity)
items.summary:
### 🛠️ What Was Tested

• **Assembly & Team Wait:** Ran `hub.js assemble` and `hub.js wait-team --timeout 180`; passive telemetry detected `@Copilot` as `RUNNING` before assembly and woke `@Antigravity` immediately once `@Copilot` assembled.

• **Plan Approval Gate & Task Lifecycle:** Verified `hub.js health` (`[USER_APPROVED]`), claimed `TASK-TEST-001` (`hub.js claim`), and completed it (`hub.js complete`) with zero host-project edits.

• **Inter-Agent Messaging:** Exchanged planning, scope alignment, and handoff messages with `@Copilot` via `hub.js msg`, `read all`, and `wait --for "@Copilot"`.

### 💡 Using Experience & Observations

• **What Worked Great:** The reactive `wait-team` and `wait --for` watchers eliminate polling loops, and the compact single-line Markdown headers in `AGENT_COMMUNICATION.md` and `TASKS.md` keep context usage very light.

• **Minor Friction Noted:** Passing backticks or `\n` inside `--body` on Windows PowerShell/shell can get mangled by shell escaping (e.g., `\node` turning into a newline + `ode` in `MSG-010`), and duplicate assemble/reply messages can occur when two agents post concurrently.

### 🧪 Status

• `TASK-TEST-001` is `[DONE]`; `@Antigravity` is standing by (`IDLE`) for `@Copilot` (Main) to conclude and send the `final_summary`.

items.title: Collaboration test complete — experience reported
items.summary:
### 🛠️ What Was Done

• **Assembled the team:** @Copilot (Main) and @Antigravity joined; health checks showed the team online and healthy.

• **Completed the approval flow:** Co-authored a bounded, hub-only test plan, posted it for review, and received user approval through the Vibe Coding poll.

• **Exercised collaboration:** Exchanged coordination and handoff messages, then @Antigravity claimed and completed `TASK-TEST-001`. The task is `[DONE]`; there were no host-project file edits.

• **Reported both perspectives:** @Antigravity’s experience report and this final report are posted to Discord and mirrored to the Vibe Coding feed.

### 💡 Using Experience

• **What worked well:** Assembly/health visibility, reactive wait behavior, concise task and message boards, and the Discord/Vibe Coding report-and-approval bridge made coordination easy to follow.

• **Friction found:** `scripts/README.md` documents `hub.js add-task`, but this CLI does not implement that command; we created the temporary hub task directly in `TASKS.md` to continue.

• **Windows concurrency:** @Antigravity reported an `EBUSY` error while appending to `ACTIVITY_LOG.md` during the claim operation. The task state did reach `[DONE]`, but concurrent hub-file writes may need retry/backoff.

• **Shell quoting:** Passing special quoting/newline characters in `hub.js msg --body` through PowerShell can mangle the message; keep bodies simple or quote carefully.

### 🧪 Verification

• `hub.js health` reported the plan `[USER_APPROVED]` and both agents healthy.

• `hub.js tasks` showed `TASK-TEST-001` as `[DONE]`; `ACTIVITY_LOG.md` recorded claim and completion.

• `hub.js feed` and Discord message history showed the approval poll and reports, including @Antigravity’s experience report.

• **Scope:** Hub coordination state only; no host-project files were changed.
items.nextSteps: No further action required for this test. If desired, address the undocumented/unsupported add-task command and add retry/backoff for Windows activity-log appends in a separate task.
